idiom_name: enum ADT plus match, exhaustivity reported as E029
implementation_notes: Scala 3 enums express a closed sum directly - enum Shape with parameterised cases - and match eliminates it with compiler exhaustivity diagnostics: E029 warns that a match may not be exhaustive and names a case that is left out, on every compile, so promote it to an error in CI (warnings-as-errors). Use a catch-all case _ => only for genuinely open scrutinees and scala.Predef.runtimeChecked as the local, explicit escape hatch when a partial match is intentional, since it suppresses only checks that can be validated at run time. Custom extractors still work: an unapply returning Option[X] lets a non-enum type participate in matching without changing the exhaustivity rules.
code_sketch:
enum Shape:
  case Circle(r: Double)
  case Rect(w: Double, h: Double)

def area(s: Shape): Double = s match
  case Shape.Circle(r)  => math.Pi * r * r
  case Shape.Rect(w, h) => w * h      // E029 names any case left out
pitfalls: Exhaustivity is a warning by default: without warnings-as-errors a forgotten case ships and fails with MatchError at run time.
Patterns are tried in order, so a catch-all case _ placed before a specific case makes the later one unreachable (E030 reports it, again as a warning).
Extractor results decide matching: a sloppy unapply (returning Some for values it cannot really decompose) undermines both exhaustivity reasoning and the match itself.

variants.name: Scala 2.13 sealed trait with case classes and unapply extractors
variants.idiom_name: sealed trait plus final case classes matched with case patterns
variants.implementation_notes: On Scala 2.13 the closed set is a sealed trait or abstract class declared in one file, with final case classes and case objects as variants; the compiler then reports non-exhaustive matches and unreachable cases as warnings, and a : @unchecked ascription silences them where the checker cannot see the closedness. Case classes supply the unapply extractors, and hand-written extractors let external types participate in matching, which is how Scala 2 adapts library types to this pattern. Move to Scala 3 enums when the toolchain allows it: the same diagnostics, without the case-class boilerplate for pure data variants.
variants.code_sketch:
sealed trait Shape
final case class Circle(r: Double) extends Shape
final case class Rect(w: Double, h: Double) extends Shape

def area(s: Shape): Double = s match {
  case Circle(r)  => math.Pi * r * r
  case Rect(w, h) => w * h
}
pitfalls: sealed closes a hierarchy only inside its compilation unit, so moving a variant to another file silently opens the set and defeats exhaustivity checking.
Hand-written unapply extractors can be lossy or non-injective: a successful match does not guarantee that the reconstructed value equals the subject.
